package_info.why_malicious: The 3CXDesktopApp installers for both Windows and macOS were trojanized to include a multi-stage malware loader. The compromised application, signed with a legitimate code signing certificate, downloads and executes additional payloads, ultimately leading to the deployment of an information-stealing infostealer DLL. This behavior is not expected in legitimate software and constitutes a supply chain attack affecting all users of the compromised versions.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon application launch or during normal operation)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The trojanized binary contains code that, after launch, downloads ICO files from github.com/IconStorages/images, extracts appended base64-encoded payloads, and writes/loads a next-stage DLL.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads ICO files from a remote GitHub repository, extracts and decodes base64-encoded data appended to these files, writes the decoded payload to disk, and loads it as a DLL for further execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate VOIP applications do not download and execute code from external sources, especially from image files hosted on GitHub.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would be to load only signed, trusted code included in the installer. Downloading and executing code from external, non-3CX-controlled sources is highly abnormal.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Auto-updaters may download signed updates, but not arbitrary code hidden in image files from third-party repositories.
key_indicators: Extracts and decodes appended base64 data
Loads decoded data as executable code (DLL)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The loaded DLL acts as an infostealer, harvesting system information, browser data, and potentially credentials, then exfiltrating this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure (e.g., akamaitechcloudservices.com, azureonlinestorage.com, msedgepackageinfo.com, etc.).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects sensitive information from the infected system, including browser data and credentials, and sends this data via HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating user data is a classic infostealer behavior and is never legitimate in a VOIP client.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A VOIP client should not access browser data, credentials, or send sensitive information to unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this behavior is always malicious in this context.
key_indicators: Sends data to non-3CX, attacker-controlled domains

attack_chain.action: User installs or updates 3CXDesktopApp with a trojanized installer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code embedded in the application binary

attack_chain.action: Trojanized application, upon launch, downloads ICO files from GitHub and extracts/decodes a next-stage payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loading and execution of the next-stage infostealer DLL

attack_chain.action: Extracted DLL is loaded and executed, harvesting sensitive data and exfiltrating it to attacker infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data theft and potential further compromise

behavioral_signatures: Application downloads ICO or image files from GitHub or non-standard sources at runtime
Extraction and decoding of base64 data from image files
Dynamic loading of DLLs not present in the original installer
Unexpected HTTPS POST requests to non-3CX domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for 3CXDesktopApp processes making network requests to GitHub repositories or the listed suspicious domains, especially for ICO/image file downloads. Detect extraction and execution of code from downloaded image files. Flag any dynamic DLL loading from files not present in the original installer. Alert on any exfiltration of browser data or credentials to non-3CX domains. Correlate with known malicious file hashes and installer filenames.
